question:
You are near the money bubble with 16bb UTG1. What hand should you jam?

Answer Choices:
A. QJs
B. None of these 
C. 99
D. AJo
E. AKo

2.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I lean toward E. AKo here. With only 16bb UTG1 on the bubble, our jamming range has to be tight and value-heavy; AKo is the clearest premium that both blocks strong calling hands and retains solid equity when called, while the bubble pressure should generate enough folds to make the jam +EV. The other options feel either too loose (QJs) or vulnerable to domination (AJo).

5.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the answer here is C. 99. With 16bb UTG1 near the bubble, we're looking for a hand that has solid equity against calling ranges (which will be tight but still include some overcards and lower pairs). 99 blocks a lot of the lower pairs that might call lighter and has good set-mining potential if it gets called, while also having fold equity against marginal holdings. Suited hands like QJs lose too much value when dominated, and AJo/AKo can run into better aces or get in rough against the top of the calling range. This feels like the hand that balances value and fold equity best in this exact spot.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I lean toward E. AKo here. With 16bb UTG1 near the bubble you're mostly looking for hands that have strong equity when called and can also fold out enough dead money from the blinds and shorter stacks behind. AKo blocks a ton of the calling range (AK, AQ, KK, AA) while still being ahead of most of the resteal/jam hands that will show up, and it plays well postflop if somehow we get called and see a flop. The suited connectors and medium pairs are more speculative and risk running into bigger pairs or dominated situations more often from early position. AJo is just a little too weak to jam into the whole table. So AKo feels like the clearest jam candidate among the options.

9.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I lean toward E. AKo here. With only 16bb UTG1 near the bubble, our opening range has to stay extremely tight to avoid getting snapped off by the big stacks behind, and AKo is the clearest value jam that still has massive equity against calling ranges while denying equity to the resteal-heavy players to our left. The suited connectors and medium pairs feel too vulnerable to domination or races that we don’t want to flip for our tournament life this close to the money, whereas AKo plays well post-bubble if we do get called.

14.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: With 16bb near the bubble from UTG1 I would jam AJo. It has solid equity against calling ranges, blocks a lot of the hands that would call a jam, and the bubble pressure plus fold equity from later positions makes it +EV while still being strong enough to show down if called. The suited hands and medium pairs feel riskier here because they play worse multiway or against tighter calling ranges.

13.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I lean toward C. 99 here. At 16bb UTG1 near the bubble, a medium pocket pair has the right combination of fold equity and showdown value against the tighter calling ranges that will face an early-position jam; suited connectors like QJs or broadway hands like AJo risk domination too often, while AKo is probably better off as a raise-fold to preserve some post-bubble playability. 99 seems like the cleanest jam candidate from the list.

17.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: With 16bb UTG1 near the bubble, I lean toward jamming E. AKo. It's the strongest hand listed, has excellent equity against calling ranges that will be tighter this close to the money, and the blocker effects on AA/KK help when we do get action. The other options either play worse postflop if called or have more domination issues. I'd rather overjam a premium than risk folding equity leaking with a marginal hand.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: With 16bb near the bubble, ICM pressure tightens EP jamming ranges significantly versus a pure chipEV push/fold chart. Standard non-ICM 15-17bb UTG1 ranges already exclude QJs and are marginal on AJo; ICM makes both clear folds. 99 is also a marginal or -EV jam once the big-stack calling ranges and ICM penalty are factored in. AKo remains a clear jam in all models. Therefore the only correct choice among the listed hands is E.

16.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: E. AKo

With 16bb UTG1 near the bubble, AKo stands out as the clearest jam candidate among the options. It has strong equity against calling ranges (dominating AJ/KQ and flipping vs pairs), blocks a lot of premium hands that might otherwise call lighter, and maintains fold equity from the big blind and shorter stacks who are trying to ladder. QJs and AJo are too dominated or flippy to justify the jam this early in the payout structure, while 99 risks running into overpairs without the same blocker value. AKo maximizes both raw equity and the chance of picking up the blinds uncontested before we get much shorter.
